articles.headline: Rams' McVay unsure about Nacua's status for Week 3 vs. Broncos
articles.description: Sean McVay said he doesn't know wide receiver Puka Nacua's game status for Week 3 against the Broncos, but the Rams' head coach said he's hopeful Nacua will play.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Sean McVay said he doesn't know wide receiver Puka Nacua's game status for Week 3 against the Denver Broncos, but the Los Angeles Rams' head coach said he's hopeful Nacua will play.

"If he's ready to go, great," McVay said. "If not, then we'll continue to roll."

Nacua was added to the Rams' injury report Friday with a hip injury. On Saturday, McVay said Nacua was dealing with "a little bit of soreness" in his groin and would not practice that day. McVay said Nacua's injury isn't related to the psoas injury that caused him to miss time during training camp.

McVay said Tuesday that when skill position players are dealing with soft tissue injuries, "You're going to err on the side of caution."

Nacua did a pregame warmup Monday night before the Rams' 28-6 victory over the New York Giants but was inactive.

In the Rams' season opener, Nacua led the Rams with five catches for 74 yards on nine targets.

articles.headline: 2026 NFL awards tracker: Odds for MVP, Rookie of the Year and more
articles.description: Who are the favorites to win seasonlong honors? Here are the odds for MVP, Rookie of the Year and more.
articles.body:
After two weeks of stellar play, Josh Allen has taken control of the NFL MVP odds board, leading the way at +290 after coming into the campaign with +600 favorite odds. The 2024 MVP has taken some action at DraftKings, but his short price the entire time is likely not making him a liability at most sportsbooks across the marketplace.

The two biggest positive movers following Week 2 were Brock Purdy and Patrick Mahomes, who have both made it to a second-best +800 from 13-1 and 15-1 a week prior, respectively. Joe Burrow and Lamar Jackson round out the top five, tied at +850. Mahomes is also the odds-on favorite to win Comeback Player of the Year at -220.

Arguably the biggest shakeup to the MVP odds board came due to several key injuries: Caleb Williams (+600 going into Week 2), Jaxson Dart (35-1) and Jayden Daniels (45-1) all left their games injured and are no longer on the odds board at time of publishing. Although it's possible all three avoided season-ending injuries, DraftKings Sportsbook director Johnny Avello told ESPN that they are keeping them off the board "as a precaution" until they know the full extent of the prognoses.

Williams has racked up significant liability at several sportsbooks, including BetMGM, which lists him as its largest caution.

articles.headline: Estêvão on reduced game time at Chelsea: 'I try to seize every opportunity I have'
articles.description: Estêvão says he is focused only on what he can control after struggling for game time at Chelsea under new manager Xabi Alonso.
articles.body:
Estêvão says he is focused only on what he can control after struggling for game time at Chelsea under new manager Xabi Alonso.

The Brazilian winger has started only twice so far this season, on both occasions in the Carabao Cup.

He has been limited to just four late substitute appearances in the Premier League totalling 23 minutes and as such has not enjoyed the kind of impact that marked his debut campaign.

Alonso has favoured a front three of João Pedro, Cole Palmer and summer signing Morgan Rogers and all three have been key figures, scoring 10 goals between them, despite a mixed start to the manager's reign.

"I think every coach has their own way of playing," Estevao told a press conference while on international duty with Brazil. "Of course, we work every day, I give my best every day and that's what I do.

"We have quality players at Chelsea, so what I do is focus on what I can control. I try to give my best in training, when I get an opportunity I try to give my best. It goes day after day."

The 19-year-old was a revelation last season and his introduction following his move from Palmeiras in the summer of 2025 was one of the only high points of a disappointing campaign for the club.

Highlights included a winning goal deep into stoppage time against Liverpool, who were the reigning Premier League champions at the time, and a brilliant individual strike in the 3-0 Champions League victory over Barcelona.

- Andre Villas-Boas hits back at John Terry's plane story: 'I see it different'

- Xabi Alonso joins unwanted managerial group after heavy Brentford defeat

- Lamine Camara better off in Monaco, ex-Chelsea midfielder says

He scored eight times in 36 appearances in all competitions en route to quickly winning over supporters at Stamford Bridge, who frequently sang his name.

Despite the team's poor defensive record so far under Alonso, they have mostly impressed going forward, scoring 18 times in seven matches, with Pedro, Palmer and Rogers especially catching the eye and thus limiting Estevao's opportunities.

"I try to seize every opportunity I have, I try to control everything I can and I leave it in God's hands and I trust myself a lot too," he said.

He was brought on three minutes from the end of Chelsea's defeat to west London rivals Brentford on Friday, with the team trailing 2-0. They conceded a further goal to eventually lose 3-0.

articles.headline: Red Sox commit to Chad Tracy, Craig Breslow through 2030
articles.description: The Red Sox signed Chad Tracy to a three-year contract as manager while also exercising the 2029 and 2030 options on chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox, who are heading to the postseason following a remarkable run over the second half of the season, rewarded the two chief architects of that turnaround on Tuesday.

Boston removed the interim tag and named Chad Tracy the 49th manager in team history, signing him to a three-year contract that will run through the 2029 season, with a club option for 2030. The Red Sox also announced that it has exercised the 2029 and 2030 options on chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.

The elevation of the 41-year-old Tracy comes after the Red Sox secured a wild-card spot in the playoffs on Sunday. Tracy took over in April after former manager Alex Cora was fired following a 10-17 start to the season.

Tracy has since guided the Red Sox to a 74-55 record, which included a 15-game win streak that tied the franchise record set in 1946. Boston's 27-3 (.900) record from July 3 through Aug. 7 was the best 30-game span in franchise history.

It's a remarkable turnaround for a team that was 32-46 and 15 1/2 games back in the American League East race on June 24.

"Craig and Chad are two exceptionally talented leaders who have earned these opportunities in very different ways," Red Sox president Sam Kennedy said in a statement. "Over the last three years, we have watched Craig bring clarity, discipline, and conviction to the work of building our baseball operation. Chad was asked to step into a difficult situation with little notice, but the trust he immediately commanded at the major league level was earned through years of work across our organization.

"What this team has accomplished over the past several months has been historic. Results matter greatly in this business, but so do judgment, character, and the ability to bring out the best in others. Craig and Chad have demonstrated all of those qualities, and they have earned our confidence in leading us forward."

Breslow, 46, was hired in October 2023. A 2013 World Series champion with Boston, he is only the fourth former Red Sox player to lead the club's baseball operations efforts.

In his three seasons in the role, the Red Sox have gone 254-226 (.529), the third-best record in the AL.

Tracy served as the manager of the Red Sox's Triple-A team in Worcester since 2022, leading the WooSox to a winning record in each of his four full seasons as manager. That came after seven previous years managing in the Los Angeles Angels minor league system.

A third-round pick by the Texas Rangers in the third round of the 2006 draft out of Pepperdine University, Tracy also played eight professional seasons (2006-13) in the Rangers, Colorado Rockies and Kansas City Royals organizations.

articles.headline: Yankees don't expect Aaron Judge (calf) back for wild card
articles.description: Aaron Judge is not expected to be available for the Yankees' wild-card series as he continues to recover from a calf strain.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone said he does not expect to have Aaron Judge available for the Wild Card series next week, though he did not completely rule out the star right fielder recovering from his calf strain in time to play.

"We're planning on him not being a part of that," Boone said Tuesday before the Yankees hosted the Tampa Bay Rays for a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.

Judge was placed on the injured list with a right calf strain Friday, two days after exiting a game against the Minnesota Twins with the injury. Judge and the team declined to specify the severity of the injury through the weekend. On Tuesday, Boone labeled it a "moderate grade" strain. He said Judge received a PPP injection Monday and will avoid physical activity over the "next couple days."

"You hear all the time with injuries, we get ranges," Boone said. "Two to four weeks, four to six, all these things. There are ranges for a reason, and we're at a point in the year where obviously we push it a little bit if that was in play. But that's a week away so I'm not expecting it, but I'm not ruling it out either."

Judge, 34, sustained the injury in his seventh game back after missing more than three months with a fractured rib. The three-time MVP returned without going on a rehab assignment and went 4 for 23 with 13 strikeouts, one walk, and one home run in 24 plate appearances. He will likely finish his injury-plagued campaign with a .241 batting average, 18 home runs and an .871 OPS in just 66 games after two historic MVP seasons.

Heliot Ramos will start in right field for the fourth straight game since Judge's absence in Tuesday's opener. Spencer Jones is another option to play right field in the postseason should Trent Grisham, who is on the injured list with a hamstring injury, return to play center field.

The Rays entered Tuesday's doubleheader with a magic number of one to clinch the American League East title with seven games remaining. Barring a Rays collapse, the Yankees will host the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card series for the second consecutive year.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Sleepers, breakouts and busts for 2026-27
articles.description: Which fantasy basketball players are going to exceed expectations in 2026-27? Who will disappoint? Who is ready to take things to an elite level? Our experts list their picks.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーバスケットボール：2026-27シーズンのスリーパー、ブレイクアウト、バスト候補
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-27シーズンに期待以上の活躍を見せるファンタジーバスケットボール選手は誰か？失望させるのは誰か？トップレベルへ飛躍する準備ができているのは誰か？専門家が注目選手を挙げます。
articles.body:
Putting together a winning fantasy basketball roster starts with a great draft. And to have a great draft, you need to know which players to go after and which to avoid.

So which players will out-produce their average draft position (ADP) this season? Who will take their game to another level? And which players are the biggest risk to take a step backward?

Our fantasy basketball experts André Snellings, Eric Moody, Eric Karabell, Jim McCormick, Steve Alexander and Michael F. Florio offer their top sleepers, breakouts and busts for the 2026-27 NBA season.

Sleepers

Sleeper: A player who will far surpass his average draft position (ADP) in standard ESPN leagues.

Naz Reid, C/PF, Charlotte Hornets

Snellings: Reid was the NBA Sixth Man of the Year two seasons ago and had carved out a role with the Timberwolves as essentially a starter that had to come off the bench due to the depth of frontline talent in Minnesota. With his trade to the Hornets, Reid has the opportunity to show that he can produce even more as a full-time starter. Reid is an efficient scorer, a strong rebounder and defender, and one of the best 3-point shooting big men in the league. Particularly in category leagues, he is poised to return fantasy value far beyond where is selected in most drafts.

Alexander: Reid has always been one of my favorite under-the-radar players and he'll have new life this season, hopefully starting for the Hornets. I wish he was a better free throw shooter (72.8% for his career), but he only shot 1.6 of them per game last year, meaning the low volume won't hurt you too bad in that category. I expect all of his numbers to get a boost this year and he's played between 68 and 81 games in six straight seasons. The only concern is his usage rate while playing alongside Coby White, Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller, but there should be enough to go around for Reid to eat.

Julius Randle, PF, Brooklyn Nets

Karabell: Randle's numbers and fantasy value fell quite a bit during two seasons with the Timberwolves, especially in rebounds, but there is little holding him back from high usage and big fantasy value with the barren Nets. Look at what Randle achieved statistically during his Knicks seasons, and expect a return to at least 24 PPG, 10 RPG and 5 APG for the other New York team, easily outproducing his tepid ADP, which always seemed out of line with his actual production.

Caleb Wilson, SF, Chicago Bulls

Florio: The No. 4 overall pick in this years NBA draft hit the ground running this summer. Wilson averaged 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.5 blocks per game in the Summer League. That is after putting up similar numbers at North Carolina last year. He has apparently been turning heads in workouts with LeBron James, too. He will start at power forward on a Bulls team that has lots of opportunities up for grabs, both in terms of scoring and rebounding. articles.headline: Expected fantasy points (xFP): 2026 leaderboard for TEs
articles.description: xFP focuses solely on opportunity. Here are the leaders for 2026.
articles.body:
Expected fantasy points (xFP) strips away player talent and efficiency and focuses solely on opportunity.

FORP -- fantasy points over replacement player -- is the difference between a player's actual fantasy point total (FF points) and his xFP (or expected total).

Tight end adjustments are made as follows:

Rushing attempts: No change

Rushing yardage: Rush attempts multiplied by a rusher's expected yardage based on position and rush direction

Rushing touchdowns: Rushing xTD

Targets: No change

Receptions: Targets multiplied by a receiver's expected catch rate based on depth of throw, location and position

Receiving yardage: Targets multiplied by a receiver's expected yardage based on depth of throw, location and position

Receiving touchdowns: Receiving xTD

Two-point conversions: xTD multiplied by the league average 2-point rate

Fumbles lost: Touches multiplied by the league average rate

Return touchdowns: Excluded due to extreme rareness and randomness

articles.headline: NBA Rank 2026, players Nos. 100-51: Four rookies make their debuts
articles.description: We're revealing our top 100 players in the league for the 2026-27 season. Which players broke into Nos. 100 to 51? Which stars fell?
articles.headlineJa: NBAランキング2026（100位〜51位）：ルーキー4選手が初ランクイン
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-27シーズンのリーグトップ100選手を発表。51位から100位に食い込んだ選手は？ランクを落としたスター選手は？
articles.body:
NBA Rank is back! With less than one month until opening night, let's start counting down the league's best players for 2026-27.

How many rookies landed in our top 100? Which stars who changed teams this summer are climbing our rankings? Where will the defending champion New York Knicks check in?

Our countdown begins with players Nos. 100-51 and continues Wednesday with Nos. 50-11 and Thursday with our expert panel's predictions for this season's top 10.

And that expert panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition.

In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list.

That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

100. Luguentz Dort

G | Atlanta Hawks

Age: 27

2025 NBA Rank: 64

The Dorture Chamber heads southeast, where the Hawks will be downright scary on the wings with Dort, Jalen Johnson and Dyson Daniels. Dort is still one of the league's most physical defenders and is entering the final year of his contract (at $18.2 million), so he'll be motivated in a new environment. His 3-point shooting fell off last season after two years at a 40% clip with the Thunder. Even if last season was a regression to the mean, the physicality Dort brings is the sell for the Hawks. -- Vincent Goodwill

Signature stat: Dort defended 2026 All-Stars for 1,238 matchups last season, the third most in the NBA.

Fantasy projection: 9.6 PTS, 3.8 REB, 1.0 STL

99. RJ Barrett

G | Toronto Raptors

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: 100

Barrett, the No. 3 pick in the 2019 draft, is a reliable secondary scorer who creates advantages with downhill attacks and plays well off lead options. Though the Toronto native hasn't developed into a franchise wing because of his mediocre outside shot and limited defensive impact, he thrilled his hometown fans in May with the signature moment of his seven-year career. When Barrett bounced home a last-second 3-pointer to beat the Cavaliers and force Game 7 in the Raptors' first-round playoff series, fans indulged in their most raucous celebration since the 2019 championship parade. -- Ben Golliver

Signature stat: Barrett shot 64% on layups and dunks last season, best in a season in his career and up from 55% in 2024-25, per GeniusIQ tracking.

Fantasy projection: 19.7 PTS, 5.6 REB, 3.9 AST

98. Jalen Suggs

G | Orlando Magic

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 59
